text:
emma_support: FinLedger (customer) opened a ticket — seeing intermittent 429 bursts in prod starting ~2026-03-17 03:20 UTC. Bursts appear aligned to their token rotation window. Attaching header snippets and short logs they pasted.

finledger_ops: copy of response headers they grabbed: 
```http
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 120
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1881002060
# no Retry-After header present in these samples
```

finledger_ops: sample ingress log (scrubbed):
```
[03:20:00.123] src=10.14.64.8 api_key=acct_finledger shard=eu-west-1 req_id=abc123 method=POST path=/v1/generate status=200 latency_ms=34
[03:20:00.456] src=10.14.64.8 api_key=acct_finledger req_id=abc124 status=429 latency_ms=1
[03:20:00.789] src=10.14.64.9 api_key=acct_finledger req_id=abc125 status=429 latency_ms=2
[03:20:01.001] src=10.14.64.8 api_key=acct_finledger req_id=abc126 status=200 latency_ms=30
```

sam_sre: initial thought — looks like a burst exactly when they rotate tokens / refresh credentials. Two things to check quickly: (1) Are they jittering token refreshes? lots of clients refreshing at the same minute -> minute-boundary fanout. (2) Are they behind an upstream NATing proxy that collapses many client IPs and confuses any per-IP heuristics?

jia_engineer: @finledger_ops can you confirm whether the requests are from a pool of client machines behind a single egress IP (eg. lambda VPC / proxy)? Also paste X-Forwarded-For from a 429 response if you have it.

finledger_ops: yes — multiple workers on our side go through a shared edge proxy. We rotate short-lived credentials every 60s so you might be right about sync. X-Forwarded-For shows the same internal IP in all samples.

sam_sre: two concurrent failure modes to consider: per-key RPM/TPM exhaustion and upstream concurrency causing thrifted requests to arrive bunched at our edge. Even though our throttles are per-API-key, backend admission and some protective fallback (e.g. soft global concurrency limit per IP) can amplify.

sam_sre: quick repro you can try from your environment to confirm minute-boundary fanout: add jitter and compare. Example script (bash) to simulate many clients rotating at the same second:
```bash
for i in $(seq 1 100); do
  (sleep 0.$((RANDOM%50)); curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}s\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate) &
done; wait
```
If you run with no jitter (sleep 0) you should see higher 429 rate at the exact second.

emma_support: also double-check that your client honors Retry-After and backoff. I see a few traces where the client immediately retries and triggers a retry loop.

jia_engineer: can you turn on request-level debug logs on your side and share a 30s window around a rotation? We want request timestamps, api_key, src ip, and any token refresh logs. If you can't share, we can capture anonymized counts per-second.

finledger_ops: we can produce per-second counts. attaching short CSV in ticket.

sam_sre: mitigation tips until root cause fixed: 
- Add random jitter to token refresh +/- 10–30s so rotations don't align.
- Add client-side concurrency limits (max inflight per worker).
- Ensure long-lived connections / HTTP keep-alive so you don't force new handshakes that line up.
- Respect Retry-After and exponential backoff.
- If you must rotate at 60s TTL, stagger refresh across instances using a consistent hashing offset.

sam_sre: platform-side quick checks we ran: 
- Confirmed per-key rate limit counters show spikes matching their api_key at rotation times.
- No recent quota bump logs.
- Edge proxy reported many connections from same egress IP cluster at those seconds.

deploy-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-0317-4927 — triage assigned to eng-oncall.

emma_support: next actions agreed: finledger to run repro script with and without jitter and attach per-second counts; we (SRE) will enable a temporary debug trace for their api_key for 1 hour and correlate; engineering to review whether any conservative per-IP protective heuristics are overaggressive for proxied customers.

finledger_ops: ack — will run repro in next 30m and paste results. thanks for the quick triage :thumbsup:

sam_sre: long-term fixes we might propose to product: exposed "token-rotation-jitter" best-practice in docs + a warning in our onboarding when we detect short TTLs + consider Relaxed NAT handling path for customers behind large NAT pools.

jia_engineer: logging checklist I need from you: per-second request counts, X-Forwarded-For sample, token-refresh timestamps, client retry config. If you can include a small pcap of a 5s window that would be golden but optional.

finledger_ops: will send the counts and X-Forwarded-For. pcap not possible right now.

emma_support: closing loop here — keeping thread open until we see repro data. Thanks all.
